did_you_know.text: Beersheba was an important settlement in southern Canaan, near the edge of the desert. Before beginning a major journey, Jacob pauses there to worship God and seek guidance.
Repeating the name “Jacob, Jacob” makes the call feel urgent and personal. In the Bible, such repetition sometimes appears at important moments.

The phrase “Joseph will place his hand over your eyes” is understood as a promise that Joseph will be with his father at his death and close his eyes. It is an ancient way of describing an honorable final farewell.
The carts sent by Pharaoh were not only a gesture of honor; they were also a practical way to transport a large family, children, women, and possessions.
Serah, Asher’s daughter, is one of the very few women mentioned in this family list. Her name appears again in the list of Israelite families in the Book of Numbers.

On, the city of Potiphera, is usually identified with Heliopolis, an important Egyptian religious center associated with sun worship. This shows that Joseph had joined a highly respected Egyptian priestly family.
The number 66 refers to the members of Jacob’s family who came from Canaan, not including the sons’ wives. Joseph and his sons are counted separately because they were already living in Egypt.
The number 70 includes Joseph and his two sons, who were born in Egypt. The ancient Greek translation of the Torah gives the number 75, probably because it includes additional relatives of Joseph.
Goshen is usually identified with a fertile area in the eastern Nile Delta, well suited for grazing. It was therefore a fitting place for a family arriving with many flocks.
Jacob and Joseph’s reunion is described with prolonged weeping because they had been separated for many years. The story emphasizes that family bonds survived distance and time.
According to the story, Egyptians regarded shepherds as culturally or religiously unacceptable. This attitude helped Jacob’s family settle separately in Goshen and preserve its way of life.
